source_evidence.observation: For a sub-gaussian random variable X, the displayed equation is ‖X − E X‖_{ψ₂} ≤ ‖X‖_{ψ₂} + ‖E X‖_{ψ₂}.
The proof recalls that ‖·‖_{ψ₂} is a norm and explicitly says that the displayed inequality is obtained by the triangle inequality.
A random variable satisfying the equivalent sub-gaussian properties is called sub-gaussian, and its sub-gaussian norm is defined by ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The source states that ‖·‖_{ψ₂} is a norm on the space of sub-gaussian random variables.
The source treats E X as a constant random variable when discussing its ψ₂ norm.

definitions_and_conventions: For a sub-gaussian random variable Y, ‖Y‖_{ψ₂} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(Y²/t²) ≤ 2}.
The functional ‖·‖_{ψ₂} is used as a norm on the space of sub-gaussian random variables, so its triangle inequality applies.
E X denotes the expectation of X and is regarded in the displayed norm as the corresponding constant random variable.
implicit_context: The equation occurs in the proof of Lemma 2.6.8 on centering a sub-gaussian random variable.
The subtraction X − E X is subtraction of the constant random variable E X from X.
The norm of the additive inverse of the constant random variable E X equals ‖E X‖_{ψ₂}, as part of the inherited norm structure.

details: The left side is the ψ₂ norm of the centered random variable X − E X.
The right side is the sum of the separate ψ₂ norms of X and the constant random variable E X.
Centering is performed by subtracting the expectation E X.
Equation (2.20) is the triangle-inequality step in the centering argument; it does not itself supply the later bound on ‖E X‖_{ψ₂}.
The stated assumption is that X is sub-gaussian.
No independence, zero-mean assumption, unit-variance assumption, auxiliary constant, or probabilistic tail conclusion appears in Equation (2.20).

undebatable_constraints: The conclusion must be the non-strict inequality ‖X − E X‖_{ψ₂} ≤ ‖X‖_{ψ₂} + ‖E X‖_{ψ₂}.
All three norms in Equation (2.20) are ψ₂ norms, not L² norms.
The left-hand argument is the centered random variable X − E X.
The second right-hand term is the ψ₂ norm of E X viewed as a constant random variable.
The justification is the triangle inequality for the ψ₂ norm.
Equation (2.20) contains no multiplicative absolute constant and does not include the later estimate of ‖E X‖_{ψ₂}.

ambiguities.issue: The source suppresses the explicit embedding of the scalar E X into the random-variable space.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 19, printed page 30, immediately after Equation (2.20), calls a an arbitrary constant random variable and then applies that observation with a = E X.
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must choose an explicit constant-random-variable representation, but this is a representational detail and does not change the mathematical inequality.

contracts.contract_plain_english: For any sub-gaussian random variable X, subtracting its expectation is subtraction of a constant random variable. Because the ψ₂ functional is a norm, the triangle inequality gives that the ψ₂ norm of X − E X is at most the ψ₂ norm of X plus the ψ₂ norm of the constant random variable E X.
